a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that investments in its self-directed and Workplace channels drive its differentiated client acquisition funnel.
items.quote: In Wealth Management, investments in our self-directed and Workplace channels drive our differentiated client acquisition funnel.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that its intense focus on the value of advice generates movement through the funnel and allows it to capture opportunities for advisor-led assets.
items.quote: Our intense focus on the value of advice, which generates movement through the funnel, allows us to capture opportunities for advisor-led assets.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says that by leveraging the Integrated Firm it is focused on generating sustainable growth in long-term flows and fee-based revenues.
items.quote: By leveraging the Integrated Firm, we are focused on our ability to generate sustainable growth in long-term flows and fee-based revenues.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that ongoing investments in its world-class platform, including support for advisors, E*TRADE capabilities, and the workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth.
items.quote: Ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its intentional strategy is to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice.
items.quote: Our intentional strategy to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice, coupled with consistent education over the past several years, sets our franchise apart and positions us to continue to outperform.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its client acquisition funnel will continue to drive Wealth Management's performance.
items.quote: Our client acquisition funnel will continue to drive Wealth Management's superb performance.

a1.MS.reason: These passages state Morgan Stanley's strategy for driving net new asset growth through its client acquisition funnel, advice, and platform investments.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is incredibly important that investment dollars go into the wealth business to broaden and deepen the funnel flywheel, including E*TRADE product, digital asset product, workplace relationships, and financial advisors.
items.quote: It's incredibly important that we continue to understand that the investment dollars go into that wealth business to broaden and deepen the funnel flywheel

items.text: Morgan Stanley identifies private markets as a growth opportunity for asset growth and asset accumulation, citing new products such as evergreen products and lower denomination products.
items.quote: There are places that we can continue to see asset growth and asset accumulation. We're offering new products to our clients, such as evergreen products and products that allow for lower denomination size.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it has been investing in processes and systems to build robust infrastructure in order to grow broadly and meet its growth objectives.
items.quote: we've been investing in all of our processes and our systems in order to engage and make sure that we have a robust infrastructure in order to be allowed to grow broadly and meet all of our growth objectives.

a2.MS.reason: These passages state investment priorities and growth opportunities tied to broadening the wealth funnel and asset accumulation.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley cites the workplace channel as a powerful asset acquisition tool, with the reopening of the IPO market supporting results.
items.quote: The reopening of the IPO market also supported results, further evidence that our workplace channel serves as a powerful asset acquisition tool.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is using its scale to invest in broadening financial advisor capabilities including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Morgan Stanley cites strategic initiatives including the acquisition of EquityZen, expanded partnership with Carta, and collaboration with Zero Hash as laying the foundation for sustainable growth.
items.quote: Strategic initiatives such as our recent acquisition of EquityZen, expanded partnership with Carta, and collaboration with Zero Hash all reflect our commitment to innovation.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says technology and investment are driving channel migration, with workplace assets seeking advice and migrating into the advisor-led channel.
items.quote: we are seeing channel migration, and that's with technology and investment, where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice

items.text: Morgan Stanley says workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and its investments are extending its runway for growth.
items.quote: Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and we are well positioned to support these new relationships. Our investments are extending our runway for growth.

items.text: Morgan Stanley cites adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and client base as embedded in its growth plans.
items.quote: Our growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base.

a3.MS.reason: These passages identify specific levers and initiatives cited to drive net new asset growth.

a4.MS.label: different_quantity

items.text: Morgan Stanley's firmwide goals include client assets of $10 trillion plus.
items.quote: Client Assets $10 Trillion +

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it seeks to grow stand-alone wealth assets from the current $8 trillion to $10 trillion.
items.quote: with the passage of time, we seek to grow stand-alone wealth assets from the current $8 trillion to $10 trillion.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says total client assets across wealth and investment management gained ground toward its target to exceed $10 trillion.
items.quote: Total client assets across wealth and investment management climbed to over $8.2 trillion, reflecting our scale and gaining ground toward our target to exceed $10 trillion.
items.scope: Wealth and Investment Management total client assets

a4.MS.differs_because: These are targets for total client assets (a stock of assets), not a target for net new asset growth (a flow of new assets).
a4.MS.reason: No passage states a target or goal specifically for net new asset growth; the firm states goals for total client assets, a related but different quantity.

a5.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley says the funnel is working after the business had net new assets of over $350 billion in 2025.
items.quote: The funnel is working.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says the power of its client acquisition funnel is becoming increasingly evident with strong capital markets.
items.quote: With strong capital markets, the power of our client acquisition funnel is becoming increasingly evident.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says its client acquisition funnel remains unrivaled in driving industry-leading growth with $118 billion of net new assets in the first quarter of 2026.
items.quote: Our client acquisition funnel remains unrivaled in driving industry-leading growth with $118 billion of net new assets and $54 billion of fee-based flows.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says net new assets of $232 billion reflect the strength of its core business and differentiated growth opportunities created by Workplace and the integrated firm.
items.quote: net new assets of $232 billion reflect the strength of our core business and the differentiated growth opportunities created by Workplace and the integrated firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is seeing momentum as IPOs come to market, with people bringing assets to Morgan Stanley.
items.quote: we're seeing momentum as you have IPOs come to market. People are bringing their assets to Morgan Stanley.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says net new assets of $59 billion in the second quarter of 2025 included a $22 billion headwind from tax outflows.
items.quote: Net new assets in the quarter of $59 billion were inclusive of a $22 billion headwind from tax outflows and reflect growth across channels.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions, and individuals use assets for consumption.
items.quote: While flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions and individuals use assets for consumption, our pipeline and our connectivity across channels allows us to build relationships early and deepen them over time.

items.text: Morgan Stanley says the level of NNA is influenced by client behavior, seasonality, ability to attract and retain advisors and clients, capital markets, and idiosyncratic flows, and these factors could impact the growth rate of NNA.
items.quote: The level of NNA in a given period is influenced by a variety of factors, including client investment and spending behaviors, seasonality, our ability to attract and retain financial advisors and clients

items.text: Morgan Stanley says cyclical headwinds to asset aggregation are beginning to abate.
items.quote: We've talked about some of the headwinds that are going from a cyclical perspective that I think are beginning to abate.

a5.MS.reason: These passages identify both momentum/traction in the funnel and headwinds such as tax outflows, lockups, distributions, and consumption.

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), management said that by leveraging the Integrated Firm it is focused on generating sustainable growth in long-term flows and fee-based revenues: "By leveraging the Integrated Firm, we are focused on our ability to generate sustainable growth in long-term flows and fee-based revenues."

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), management said ongoing investments in its world-class platform—including investments to support advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of the workplace channel—serve as an engine for future growth: "Ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management said its intentional strategy is to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice: "Our intentional strategy to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice, coupled with consistent education over the past several years, sets our franchise apart and positions us to continue to outperform."

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said its client acquisition funnel will continue to drive Wealth Management's performance: "Our client acquisition funnel will continue to drive Wealth Management's superb performance."

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management said it is incredibly important that investment dollars go into the wealth business to broaden and deepen the funnel flywheel, including E*TRADE product, digital asset product, workplace relationships, and financial advisors: "It's incredibly important that we continue to understand that the investment dollars go into that wealth business to broaden and deepen the funnel flywheel."

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management identified private markets as a growth opportunity for asset growth and asset accumulation, citing new products such as evergreen products and lower-denomination products: "There are places that we can continue to see asset growth and asset accumulation. We're offering new products to our clients, such as evergreen products and products that allow for lower denomination size."

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management cited the workplace channel as a powerful asset acquisition tool, with the reopening of the IPO market supporting results: "The reopening of the IPO market also supported results, further evidence that our workplace channel serves as a powerful asset acquisition tool."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management said it is using its scale to invest in broadening financial advisor capabilities that are difficult for others to replicate, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending: "We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management cited strategic initiatives including the acquisition of EquityZen, an expanded partnership with Carta, and a collaboration with Zero Hash as laying the foundation for sustainable growth: "Strategic initiatives such as our recent acquisition of EquityZen, expanded partnership with Carta, and collaboration with Zero Hash all reflect our commitment to innovation."

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management said technology and investment are driving channel migration, with workplace assets seeking advice and migrating into the advisor-led channel: "we are seeing channel migration, and that's with technology and investment, where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice."

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and its investments are extending its runway for growth: "Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and we are well positioned to support these new relationships. Our investments are extending our runway for growth."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management cited adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and client base as embedded in its growth plans: "Our growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management said the funnel is working after the business had net new assets of over $350 billion in 2025: "The funnel is working."

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), management said Wealth Management net new assets of $232 billion reflect the strength of its core business and the differentiated growth opportunities created by Workplace and the integrated firm: "net new assets of $232 billion reflect the strength of our core business and the differentiated growth opportunities created by Workplace and the integrated firm."

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management said it is seeing momentum as IPOs come to market, with people bringing their assets to Morgan Stanley: "we're seeing momentum as you have IPOs come to market. People are bringing their assets to Morgan Stanley."

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), management said Wealth Management net new assets of $59 billion in the quarter were inclusive of a $22 billion headwind from tax outflows and reflected growth across channels: "Net new assets in the quarter of $59 billion were inclusive of a $22 billion headwind from tax outflows and reflect growth across channels."

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), management said flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions, and individuals use assets for consumption, but that its pipeline and connectivity across channels allow it to build relationships early and deepen them over time: "While flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions and individuals use assets for consumption, our pipeline and our connectivity across channels allows us to build relationships early and deepen them over time."

Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 30, 2026, Item 2) states that the level of net new assets in a given period is influenced by a variety of factors, including client investment and spending behaviors, seasonality, the ability to attract and retain financial advisors and clients, capital markets, and idiosyncratic flows, and that these factors could impact the growth rate of NNA: "The level of NNA in a given period is influenced by a variety of factors, including client investment and spending behaviors, seasonality, our ability to attract and retain financial advisors and clients."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), management said cyclical headwinds to asset aggregation are beginning to abate: "We've talked about some of the headwinds that are going from a cyclical perspective that I think are beginning to abate."

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James' optimism about future growth is fueled by its robust advisor recruiting pipeline, and that its unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions, strong balance sheet, and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.
items.quote: We offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture, coupled with leading technology and solutions. This value proposition, coupled with our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: The 10-K states continuous recruitment and retention of financial advisors is an important driver of success, and the firm's ability to attract high-quality advisors is based on its values-based culture, commitment to service, and unique ways it provides services to financial advisors.
items.quote: Our ability to attract high quality advisors is based on our values-based culture, our commitment to service, and the unique ways in which we provide services to our financial advisors.

items.text: Raymond James' recruiting page describes AdvisorChoice as a platform of affiliation options - Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA - each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James' best-of-both-worlds value proposition - advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions - resonates across all affiliation options, and its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is a differentiator.
items.quote: Our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said the advisor recruiting pipeline is growing significantly across all affiliation options, which he called a testament to the firm's unique culture and robust platform.
items.quote: Our advisor recruiting pipeline is growing significantly across all of our affiliation options, a testament to our unique culture and robust platform that is resonating with advisors.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James treats recruiting as a long-term marathon, not a sprint, and is not targeting advisors who move only for the highest check; the firm wants advisors who want to be there over the long term.
items.quote: It's a marathon, not a sprint... You're gonna get the advisors that are moving or not moving for the highest check, and that's not who we're targeting. We have to have a competitive check, but we want the advisors that want to be here over the long term

a1.RJF.reason: Passages contain multiple firm statements describing Raymond James' strategy for recruiting advisors (value proposition, affiliation options, long-term approach).

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James' employee advisor page says employee advisors own their book of business and are free to succeed on their terms, with no quotas and no product pushing.
items.quote: Book ownership is just the beginning... As a Raymond James employee advisor, you're free to succeed on your terms – no quotas, no product pushing.

items.text: Raymond James' independent advisor page pitches powerful independence: independent contractors can access Raymond James' full capabilities and the support of a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer.
items.quote: Powerful independence. Serve your clients and grow your independent practice without wanting for capability, expert insight or client resources.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James invests more than $1.1 billion annually in technology, including automation, process improvement and AI, to give advisers more time to deepen client relationships.
items.quote: we'll continue investing in automation, process improvement and AI as part of our more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James will not have quotas, push products, or create variable incentives to drive product growth, because that is not the firm's culture.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry contrasted Raymond James' approach: it attracts and retains advisors with unique culture, leading service and robust platform, whereas many competitors compete with the largest check; and it values independence, whereas many competitors change comp plans every year to cross-sell bank products.
items.quote: We attract and retain financial advisors with our unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check. We value independence to foster an environment where our advisors can provide objective advice to their clients, whereas many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James has the largest addressable market because it offers all affiliation options and is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, and very few firms treat advisers like clients anymore.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want... very few firms in the industry that treat advisers like clients anymore.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said competitors with similar cultures have technology investment that is a fraction of Raymond James' roughly $1 billion, making it hard for them to remain competitive on AI and tools.
items.quote: a lot of our competitors who also are focused on personal relationships, and that have similar cultures, their technology investment, for example, is a fraction of ours.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James treats recruiting as a long-term marathon and does not dial it up or down quarter by quarter, unlike other firms that lean into recruiting quarter by quarter, which he called unsustainable.
items.quote: when I hear other firms talk about, 'Oh, we think next quarter we're going to lean into recruiting and put a little bit more money into it,' it's like, well, that's not sustainable long-term recruiting.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James wants to use AI to empower advisors to better serve clients, whereas many competitors have used technology and plan to use AI to go around advisors and directly to clients.
items.quote: whereas we're really wanting to use AI to help our financial professionals and our financial advisors better serve their clients, where many of our competitors have used technology and are planning on using AI to essentially try to get around their financial advisors to go direct to their clients.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James focuses on sustainable growth and quality over quantity with a strong balance sheet, whereas many competitors focus on growth at all costs and have significantly higher leverage.
items.quote: We are focused on sustainable growth and quality over quantity, whereas many of our competitors are focused on growth at all costs. We strive to maintain a strong balance sheet with strong levels of capital and liquidity, whereas many of our competitors have significantly higher levels of leverage.

a7.RJF.reason: Passages contain firm statements contrasting Raymond James' model and offering with competitors, including wirehouses and other firms.

claims.text: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James' optimism about future growth is fueled by its robust advisor recruiting pipeline, and that its unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions, strong balance sheet, and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives: "We offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture, coupled with leading technology and solutions. This value proposition, coupled with our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives."

The fiscal 2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states continuous recruitment and retention of financial advisors is an important driver of success, and that the firm's ability to attract high-quality advisors is based on its values-based culture, commitment to service, and unique ways it provides services to financial advisors: "Our ability to attract high quality advisors is based on our values-based culture, our commitment to service, and the unique ways in which we provide services to our financial advisors."

On the earnings call for the period ended March 31, 2025 (published April 23, 2025), he said Raymond James wants to use AI to empower advisors to better serve clients, whereas many competitors have used technology and plan to use AI to go around advisors and directly to clients. This is a qualitative self-characterization, not a like-for-like numeric comparison across firms.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that through its Advisor Services segment it has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients, and that it maintains its competitive position through sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed.
items.quote: Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.

items.text: Schwab's CEO states the firm has built its advisor business around helping independent advisors grow, compete, and succeed.
items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed.

items.text: Schwab states it is deepening relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs, including lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.
items.quote: we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs. We've grown our lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded our institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform

items.text: Schwab's CEO states Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for RIAs with under $100 million AUM and that its role is to provide a platform and support ecosystem that helps RIAs support their clients and helps their firms thrive.
items.quote: Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive.

items.text: A Schwab spokesperson states that, as the largest custodian for advisors, Schwab is focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and retail investors and on investing in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow.
items.quote: Schwab is focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and retail investors. Few firms can bring together custody, trading, banking, lending, wealth management, workplace and retail investing at Schwab's scale and value - with the best client service, year after year.

a1.SCHW.reason: Schwab's own statements in filings, transcripts, and a spokesperson quote state its overall RIA custody/advisor services strategy.

a2.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states the Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.
items.quote: The Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.

items.text: Schwab states RIAs and their clients have access to its broad range of wealth services and that, as custodian, Schwab earns revenue from underlying client assets and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.
items.quote: By functioning as the custodian, Schwab earns revenue associated with the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees. In this capacity, we do not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.

items.text: Schwab states it serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.
items.quote: Today, we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support.

items.text: Schwab states Advisor Services is in a position of strength and remains a driving force for Schwab, with $5.2T in client assets, 16K advisory firms, and 3.9M households, and #1 in RIA custodial assets.
items.quote: Advisor Services is in a position of strength & remains a driving force for Schwab. $5.2T Client Assets 16K Advisory Firms Households 3.9M in RIA Custodial Assets #1

items.text: Schwab states Schwab Advisor Services provides custody, trading, and the support services of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. to independent investment advisors.
items.quote: Schwab Advisor Services provides custody, trading, and the support services of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. ("Schwab"), member SIPC, to independent investment advisors and Charles Schwab Investment Management, Inc. ("CSIM").

a2.SCHW.reason: Passages describe the RIA custody/advisor services business and its offering in Schwab's own terms.

a3.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states its strategic priority is to be the leading RIA support ecosystem, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
items.quote: The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service

items.text: Schwab states it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone, including growing lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.
items.quote: we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs. We've grown our lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded our institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform

items.text: Schwab states it is enhancing its digital experiences across RIA workflows such as move money, account open, and account maintenance, while modernizing tools on its advisor platform.
items.quote: In Advisor Services, we're continuing to enhance our digital experiences across RIA workflows like move money, account open and account maintenance while also modernizing tools on our adviser platform.

items.text: Schwab states that in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.
items.quote: In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

items.text: Schwab states it is investing in banking and lending for RIAs as the natural provider of those capabilities and is just getting started with its banking journey for RIAs.
items.quote: And the RIAs want to be able to match that, and we're the natural provider of that... I think we're just getting started with our banking journey, and I couldn't be more excited about it.

items.text: Schwab states it launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.
items.quote: In our advisor services business, we launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.

a3.SCHW.reason: Passages state Schwab's strategic priorities for the RIA/advisor services business.

a4.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that in the Advisor Services arena it competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.
items.quote: In the Advisor Services arena, we compete with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

items.text: Schwab's CEO states that RIAs compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses and that wirehouses are doing a better job of leveraging their banking capabilities.
items.quote: They do, from time to time, compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses... the wirehouses are doing a better job of leveraging their banking capabilities.

items.text: Schwab's CEO states that independent advisors are competing against wirehouses that typically have strong banks attached to their advice.
items.quote: If you put yourself in the shoes of the independent advisor, they're competing against wirehouses that typically have really strong banks attached to their advice.

a4.SCHW.reason: Schwab's 10-K and CEO statements name the competitor categories and wirehouses it competes with in the RIA custody/advisor services arena.

a5.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab's CEO states that Schwab has changed the minimums for long/short strategies and throttled growth to some extent.
items.quote: as we look to October, where we have changed the minimums for long/short and throttled growth to some extent, the growth has in no way slowed at all in terms of AS NNA.

items.text: Schwab states it limited long-short offerings to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors.
items.quote: That led the firm to limit long-short offerings only to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors.

items.text: Schwab states it is reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM.
items.quote: reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM.

items.text: A Schwab spokesperson confirms the asset minimum for client referrals in Schwab Advisor Network has changed from $2 million to $5 million, effective Jan. 5, 2027.
items.quote: the asset minimum for client referrals in Schwab Advisor Network (SAN) has changed from $2 million to $5 million, effective Jan. 5, 2027.

items.text: A Schwab spokesperson states that, following a review of Forge Global after its acquisition, Schwab has reached an agreement to divest the Forge Trust business, a self-directed IRA custodian.
items.quote: Following that review, we've reached an agreement to divest the Forge Trust business. We are committed to Forge's private markets platform and are excited about the capabilities it brings to Schwab clients.

a5.SCHW.reason: Schwab statements describe pullbacks in RIA-related areas (long/short limits, SAN referral reductions, Forge Trust divestiture); no Schwab statement in the passages says it is losing ground.

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that, through its Advisor Services segment, Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients, and that management believes Schwab can maintain its competitive position primarily through its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.
On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab's CEO stated that Schwab has built its advisor business around helping independent advisors grow, compete, and succeed.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Schwab stated it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs, including lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.

Trade press reports (published October 28, 2026) that Schwab's CEO stated Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for RIAs with under $100 million AUM and that Schwab's role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps RIAs support their clients and helps their firms thrive.

Trade press reports (published August 26, 2026) that a Schwab spokesperson stated Schwab, as the largest custodian for advisors, is focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and retail investors and on investing in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow.

The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that the Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.

The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that RIAs and their clients have access to Schwab's broad range of wealth services and that, by functioning as the custodian, Schwab earns revenue associated with the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees, and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab stated it serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.

In its May 14, 2026 investor day deck, Schwab states that Advisor Services is in a position of strength and remains a driving force for Schwab, with $5.2T in client assets, 16K advisory firms, and 3.9M households, and is #1 in RIA custodial assets.
In its May 14, 2026 investor day deck, Schwab states that Schwab Advisor Services provides custody, trading, and the support services of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. to independent investment advisors.

In its May 14, 2026 investor day deck, Schwab states its strategic priority is to be the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Schwab stated that in Advisor Services it is continuing to enhance its digital experiences across RIA workflows such as move money, account open, and account maintenance while also modernizing tools on its advisor platform.

On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), Schwab stated that in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Schwab stated it is investing in banking and lending for RIAs as the natural provider of those capabilities and that it is just getting started with its banking journey for RIAs.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Schwab stated that in its advisor services business it launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.

The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025, published February 25, 2026) states that, in the Advisor Services arena, Schwab competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), Schwab's CEO stated that RIAs from time to time compete against the wealth divisions of wirehouses and that wirehouses are doing a better job of leveraging their banking capabilities.
Trade press reports (published October 29, 2026) that Schwab's CEO stated independent advisors are competing against wirehouses that typically have really strong banks attached to their advice.
On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Schwab's CEO stated that Schwab has changed the minimums for long/short strategies and throttled growth to some extent.
Trade press reports (published October 28, 2026) that Schwab stated it limited long-short offerings to clients with at least $10 million in assets, curtailing their use by many advisors.

Trade press reports (published October 28, 2026) that Schwab stated it is reducing the Schwab Advisor Network referral network by raising the bar for participation to only clients with over $5 million and RIAs with at least $500 million in AUM.

Trade press reports (published August 24, 2026) that a Schwab spokesperson confirmed the asset minimum for client referrals in Schwab Advisor Network has changed from $2 million to $5 million, effective January 5, 2027.

a1.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill's advisor growth strategy centers on growing the sales force, with management stating an aim of 5% over the next 3 to 5 years, while noting advisor attrition is near historic lows.
items.quote: we said we are aiming for 5% over the course of the next 3 to 5 years... just keep growing the sales force. Well, adviser attrition is now at near historic lows.

items.text: Merrill adds financial advisors through its extensive training program and through experienced hiring of advisors.
items.quote: We also continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors.

items.text: Recruiting experienced advisors is not an enormous part of Merrill's strategy; management says the training program is what it can keep driving.
items.quote: we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy, but it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management

items.text: Management says it remains focused on pricing discipline, advisor productivity and long-term client relationships, drives productivity higher on newer and existing advisors, and attracts talent across new and experienced advisers.
items.quote: We remain focused on pricing discipline, adviser productivity and long-term client relationships. We're driving productivity higher on both newer and existing members of our financial advisers team, and we continue to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

items.text: Merrill states as a foundational belief that having the best advisors enables it to deliver exceptional client outcomes.
items.quote: …having the best advisors enables us to deliver exceptional client outcomes

items.text: Merrill's advisor recruiting page describes a collaborative team in a high-tech, high-touch environment and lead-generation infrastructure through Bank of America.
items.quote: At Merrill, you are supported by a collaborative team of dedicated professionals in a high-tech, high-touch environment focused on helping you take your practice to the next level.

a1.MER.reason: Multiple passages state Merrill's advisor growth strategy priorities and initiatives.

a2.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017, then returned to it after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf took over in 2023 and restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.
items.quote: The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

items.text: Merrill executives in October 2026 said recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting.

a2.MER.reason: The trade press passage describes the shift away from and later return to veteran broker recruiting.

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024; published January 16, 2025), management said it has been investing in its Wealth Management processes and systems "across the technology side, across better understanding our data, better servicing our clients in terms of investment dollars and in terms of the underlying infrastructure."

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2025; published April 11, 2025), management said it is seeing the benefits of investments it has been making into its advisor-led platform over multiple years: "we are seeing the benefits of the investments that we have been making into that platform over multiple years, including even the most recent last year."

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2025; published April 11, 2025), management said its financial advisors can offer clients world-class technology through the integrated firm: "the financial advisor is seeing the integrated firm for what it is, which is we can offer unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology".

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025; published July 16, 2025), management said its ongoing investments in its world-class platform include investments to support its advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and expansion of its workplace channel: "Ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth."

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025; published October 15, 2025), management described LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform, as an early AI use case that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with its financial advisors: "LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025; published January 15, 2026), management said it continues to invest in its Wealth segment via technology, and that its growth plans embed increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside its client base: "We continue to invest in each of our three business segments: Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology. Our growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base."

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025; published January 15, 2026), management said LeadIQ is an AI tool used on the revenue side that helps introduce its advisors to clients interested in advice: "LeadIQ, for example, which is helping us introduce our advisors to our clients who are interested in advice, that's happening using AI."

Morgan Stanley: In its FY2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025; published February 19, 2026), the company said competition in its Wealth Management segment is affected by its technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization: "our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization."

items.text: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options under the name AdvisorChoice®; financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.

items.text: Independent contractor financial advisors generally pay their own direct costs and therefore receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors; they may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.

Our independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help our advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of our support as they determine they need. Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with us directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in our Financial Institutions Division.

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: In its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 (Item 1, published November 25, 2025), Raymond James states that it offers multiple affiliation options, which it refers to as AdvisorChoice®, and that financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division: "We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division."

Raymond James Financial: In its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 (Item 1, published November 25, 2025), Raymond James states that independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and therefore receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors, and that independent contractor advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in its Financial Institutions Division: "Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors. Our independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help our advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of our support as they determine they need. Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with us directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in our Financial Institutions Division."

Raymond James Financial: On its affiliation options web page (content as of April 21, 2026), Raymond James says that through AdvisorChoice® advisors can match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, and the page lists the options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom, and flexibility: "Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that’s right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm."
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: In its 2025 Investor Day deck (published June 5, 2025), Raymond James presents the AdvisorChoice spectrum as spanning employee advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, independent advisor (ICD), banks and credit unions, IAR (corporate RIA), and RIA & custody services, and states: "The movement to 'independence' is not channel-specific."

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), Raymond James said it has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options—from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody—with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them: "we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them."

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025 (published October 22, 2025), management said recruiting success has been broad-based across all of the firm's affiliation options—the employee, independent contractor, and RIA custody channels: "The recruiting success that we've been having has really been broad-based across all of our affiliation options, the employee, independent contractor, and the RAA custody channels."

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended March 31, 2026 (published April 22, 2026), the CEO said the firm is seeing a pretty good uptick in the employee affiliation option as well, and that the mix shift he referred to relates to the comp ratio because the independent channel has a higher payout than the employee channel: "we're actually seeing pretty good uptick in the employee affiliation option as well. And the mix shift is really what I was referring to more about the comp ratio than the margin because the payout difference in the independent channel versus the employee channel."

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the fiscal third quarter of 2025 (period ended June 30, 2025, published July 23, 2025), the CEO said the firm was seeing good success across all of its affiliation options, with the acceleration rate within the independent channel probably higher, while the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA option also saw very good success: "I would say we are seeing good success across all of our affiliation options. Certainly, the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher, but we are still seeing very good success in the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA, option as well."

Raymond James Financial: Whether the mix across the affiliation models has shifted can be compared on this evidence only for the employee and independent contractor affiliation options and only at the three period-ends of September 30, 2023, September 30, 2024, and September 30, 2025. The 10-K reports employee, independent contractor, and total financial advisor headcounts on the same basis for those same three period-ends, and states that advisors in the RCS division are not included in the financial advisor metric. The available figures are headcounts—a stand-in for the mix—and no separate headcounts for the other AdvisorChoice options or any figure after September 30, 2025 were found, so the full AdvisorChoice mix cannot be compared on this evidence.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's advisor-led flows are coming from existing advisors, recruits, and workplace origination, according to CFO Sharon Yeshaya.
items.quote: Advisor-led is coming both from existing advisors as well as recruits and the origination of workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's advisor-led flows originated from new advisors attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace, according to CFO Sharon Yeshaya.
items.quote: Advisor-led flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has recruiting on the advisor-led side in addition to flows from workplace, and recruits are interested in the platform investments, according to CFO Sharon Yeshaya.
items.quote: There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in... From the advisor-led side, we do have recruiting, but we also have flows coming in from workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley reported positive recruiting trends among the drivers of strong net new assets, according to CFO Sharon Yeshaya.
items.quote: The result was supported by broad-based strength across channels, inclusive of elevated flows related to advisor-led clients, stock plan vesting events, positive recruiting trends, and self-directed clients.

a1.MS.reason: The passages state Morgan Stanley's recruiting approach and advisor-led sources (existing advisors, recruits, workplace), so these are facts.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley will increase the cash component of its advisor compensation, which it says supports its overall investment into financial advisors and simplifies its compensation program.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. We are making these changes to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings... these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: Morgan Stanley used recruiting bonus money structured as promissory notes (loans that brokers pay back to firms over time) and sought to claw back such recruiting bonus money from a former advisor.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley sued Cohen in 2021 in a dispute over promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time. Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from Cohen.

items.text: Morgan Stanley attempted to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans from a former advisor, according to a FINRA arbitration award.
items.quote: turned aside Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, along with attorney's fees and interest.

a2.MS.reason: The passages describe Morgan Stanley's advisor compensation changes and recruiting bonus loans (promissory notes/forgivable loans), so these are facts.

a3.MS.label: different_quantity

items.text: Morgan Stanley's talent development programs are designed to provide employees firm-wide with resources to achieve career goals, build management skills and lead their organizations, which the firm says supports long-term retention.
items.quote: Our talent development programs are designed to provide employees with the resources to help them achieve their career goals, build management skills and lead their organizations. We believe supporting employee development and growth contributes to long-term retention.

items.text: Morgan Stanley requires every new hire and every employee annually to certify understanding of and adherence to its Code of Conduct.
items.quote: Every new hire and every employee annually is required to certify to their understanding of and adherence to the Code of Conduct.

items.text: Morgan Stanley maintains a global training program covering cybersecurity risks and requirements for employees and consultants, including heightened security training for specialized employees and phishing simulations.
items.quote: we maintain a global training program covering cybersecurity risks and requirements, including heightened security training to specialized employees, and conduct regular phishing email simulations for our employees and consultants as preventative measures.

a3.MS.differs_because: The passages describe firm-wide employee development/training and new-hire Code of Conduct certification, not onboarding/training programs specifically for newly recruited or new financial advisors.
a3.MS.reason: The passages cover all employees/new hires generally rather than advisor-specific onboarding and training, so this is a different, wider quantity.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley reported 15,950 Wealth Management representatives at December 31, 2020.
items.quote: Wealth Management representatives 15,950 15,469 15,468 3% 3%

items.text: Morgan Stanley reported 15,469 Wealth Management representatives at September 30, 2020.
items.quote: Wealth Management representatives 15,950 15,469 15,468 3% 3%

items.text: Morgan Stanley reported 15,468 Wealth Management representatives at December 31, 2019.
items.quote: Wealth Management representatives 15,950 15,469 15,468 3% 3%

items.text: Trade press describes Morgan Stanley as having close to 15,000 high-producing financial advisors.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley is a one of the leading wealth management companies in the country, with close to 15,000 high-producing financial advisors and robust online and workplace platforms to attract new clients.

items.text: Morgan Stanley told its roughly 15,000 financial advisors about suspending participation in Forbes and Shook rankings, according to trade press.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley told its 15,000 or so financial advisors last week that, after consideration, the firm was suspending participation in Forbes and Shook advisor rankings and conferences.

a4.MS.reason: The passages state Morgan Stanley's advisor headcount figures, so this is a fact for the advisor_headcount metric.

a5.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley sponsors deferred cash-based and stock-based compensation programs for financial advisors in Wealth Management that generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions; advisor deferred compensation is generally 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.quote: including financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment, which generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions. Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.

items.text: Trade press states Morgan Stanley has for years taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation requiring years of service to vest, and advisors who leave forfeit it (golden handcuffs).
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest... forfeits that compensation, which is also known on Wall Street as golden handcuffs.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses in its 2027 advisor pay plan and is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors must generate that much more revenue for the same pay.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach... Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: For certain revenue-producing employees in Wealth Management and Investment Management, Morgan Stanley pays compensation largely on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.quote: For certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.scope: Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments

a5.MS.reason: The passages describe Morgan Stanley's deferred compensation, 2027 pay plan, and formulaic payout arrangements for advisors, so these are facts.

a6.MS.reason: The passages do not state anything about Morgan Stanley's succession and continuity planning programs for financial advisors as a retention tool; the only related mention is a board committee charter name, not an advisor program.

a7.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley CEO Edward Pick stated the adviser retention rate is above 99%.
items.quote: I'm at a place where the adviser retention rate is above 99% and the clients obviously are quite happy

a7.MS.reason: Morgan Stanley states an adviser retention rate above 99%, which is a retention rate the sub-question asks for.

a1.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill's advisor recruiting page invites advisors to join Merrill to take their advisory practice to the next level.
items.quote: Ready to take your advisory practice to the next level? Join one of the industry’s largest and most prestigious financial institutions.

items.text: Merrill's Advisor Development Program targets people interested in a wealth management career who have an entrepreneurial spirit and want to build a book of high-net-worth clients.
items.quote: If you’re interested in a career in wealth management and possess the entrepreneurial spirit - the Advisor Development Program is for you.

items.text: Merrill offers opportunities for existing advisors who already hold Series 7 and 66 licenses.
items.quote: Opportunities for existing advisors with Series 7 and 66

items.text: Merrill's CFO said the firm is recruiting experienced advisors, but that this is not an enormous part of its strategy; the training program is what it expects to keep driving.
items.quote: we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy, but it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management, Bank of America, and Merrill, and that's ultimately what we believe we can just keep driving

items.text: Merrill and the Private Bank add financial advisors through an extensive training program and experienced hiring; about one-third of Q2 net new households were added by newly trained advisors.
items.quote: We also continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors. Approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by our newly trained advisors.

items.text: Merrill continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.
items.quote: we continue to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

items.text: Merrill executives said recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting after largely pulling back at the end of 2017.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting.

items.text: Merrill and the Private Bank incurred costs of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform.
items.quote: Expense growth of 9% supported both the cost of the increase in fees as well as investment in technology and the cost of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform in Merrill and the private bank.

a1.MER.reason: Passages describe Merrill's recruiting approach and targets, including both experienced/veteran advisor recruiting and its new-advisor training program.

a2.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill's Advisor Development Program offers base salary and unlimited earning potential.
items.quote: Base salary and unlimited earning potential

a2.MER.reason: Only a partial fact is available: the ADP page states base salary and unlimited earning potential for new advisors; no passage states signing bonuses, transition packages, or forgivable loans.

a3.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill's Advisor Development Program provides industry-leading training, dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses, and coaching by a dedicated leadership team and mentorship opportunities.
items.quote: Industry leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses - Opportunities for existing advisors with Series 7 and 66 - Base salary and unlimited earning potential - High-quality leads and direct client interactions - Coaching by dedicated leadership team and mentorship opportunities

items.text: Path A, the ADP Client Associate, takes approximately 13 months including three months of licensing and progresses to ADP Financial Advisor upon full licensing.
items.quote: Obtain the SIE, Series 7 and Series 66 with career expectation to become a Merrill Financial Advisor ... Approximately 13 months including three months of licensing ... Role progresses to Merrill Advisor Development Program-Financial Advisor upon obtaining full licensing

items.text: Path B, the ADP Financial Solutions Advisor, takes approximately 13 months and develops the ability to support clients through banking and investing solutions.
items.quote: Obtain SIE, Series 7 and Series 66 and develop the ability to confidently support new and existing clients through banking and investing solutions ... Approximately 13 months

items.text: The ADP Financial Advisor stage takes approximately 1-4 years, during which advisors develop a business plan to grow their wealth management practice.
items.quote: Entry point or progress from ADP CA or ADP FSA and develop a business plan to grow your wealth management practice. ... Approximately 1-4 years

items.text: Merrill's CFO described the advisor effort as a training program that trains people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill.
items.quote: it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management, Bank of America, and Merrill

a3.MER.reason: Passages describe Merrill's Advisor Development Program and training approach for new advisors.
