a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James attributes its advisor recruiting approach to an advisor- and client-focused culture combined with leading technology and solutions, supported by its balance sheet and commitment to independence.
items.quote: We offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture, coupled with leading technology and solutions. This value proposition, coupled with our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: The firm recruits experienced, production advisors from competitors; in fiscal 2025 it recruited production advisors with prior production of over $400 million.
items.quote: in fiscal 2025, we recruited production advisors with prior production of over $400 million, which was up 21% over last year's record.

items.text: For new/trainee advisors, Raymond James offers the Wealth Management Associate Program for branch experience and the Advisor Mastery Program to begin building a client base.
items.quote: Individuals who want to become financial advisors can gain relevant branch experience through our Wealth Management Associate Program or move to our Advisor Mastery Program and begin building their client base.

items.text: Raymond James participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when affiliating with a new firm and their ability to solicit prior-firm clients.
items.quote: We participate, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting ("Protocol"), a voluntary agreement among many firms in the industry that governs... the client information that financial advisors may take with them when they affiliate with a new firm and the financial advisor's ability to solicit clients of their prior firm.

items.text: Through AdvisorChoice, advisors can match their goals to an affiliation option (Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA).
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility

items.text: Advisor Select is an employee affiliation option targeting established advisors who want to lead a team and build their own branch.
items.quote: Advisor Select® provides established advisors the full benefits of our employee channel with the independence to create their own branches

a1.RJF.reason: Passages state RJF's recruiting approach and show it targets both experienced production advisors and new/trainee advisors.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James offers loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes, with $14 million of unfunded commitments as of June 30, 2026.
items.quote: We offer loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes... We had unfunded commitments of $ 14 million for loans to financial advisors who have met such conditions as of June 30, 2026.

items.text: Unfunded commitments for loans to financial advisors were $15 million as of June 30, 2025.
items.quote: We have unfunded commitments of $ 15 million for loans to financial advisors who have met such conditions as of June 30, 2025.

items.text: Loans to financial advisors are primarily originated as part of the firm's recruiting activities.
items.quote: Loans to financial advisors are primarily comprised of loans originated as a part of our recruiting activities.

items.text: In fiscal 2025, adjusted compensation expense included amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors of $355 million, up about 11% from fiscal 2024.
items.quote: In fiscal year 2025, adjusted compensation expense included the amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors in the aggregate amount of $355 million, representing an increase of approximately 11% compared to fiscal 2024.

items.text: Raymond James says its competitive pay packages include base salary, incentive bonus, and equity compensation programs.
items.quote: Our competitive pay packages include base salary, incentive bonus, and equity compensation programs.

items.text: The firm may grant equity awards in connection with initial employment or under various retention programs.
items.quote: we may grant equity awards in connection with initial employment or under various retention programs for individuals who are responsible for contributing to our management, growth, and/or profitability.

items.text: Traditional Employee affiliation offers up to 50% payout plus employee benefits.
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee... Payout + Benefits: Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: Advisor Select affiliation offers 70-80% gross payout plus employee benefits.
items.quote: Model: Advisor Select... Payout + Benefits: 70-80% gross payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: Independent Contractor affiliation offers 81% to 90% payout.
items.quote: Model: Independent Contractor... Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***.

items.text: The firm plans to break out the upfront money amortization that hits Private Client Group compensation expense, tied to its recruiting.
items.quote: we're going to start breaking out next quarter, the upfront money amortization that hits the compensation expense in the Private Client Group business.

items.text: Raymond James states 100% of what it pays in transition assistance goes to advisor retention rather than to a seller.
items.quote: 100% of what we pay in transition assistance is going to retention versus the seller.

a2.RJF.reason: Passages describe recruiting loans, transition assistance, upfront money amortization, pay packages, equity awards at initial employment, and payout grids offered to recruited advisors.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: New/trainee advisors can gain branch experience through the Wealth Management Associate Program or move to the Advisor Mastery Program to begin building a client base.
items.quote: Individuals who want to become financial advisors can gain relevant branch experience through our Wealth Management Associate Program or move to our Advisor Mastery Program and begin building their client base.

items.text: The firm has a department providing growth-oriented tools, business coaching, and conferences and workshops for financial advisors.
items.quote: We have a department dedicated to providing growth-oriented tools and resources, including business coaching, to our financial advisors. We also offer these advisors the opportunity to participate in conferences and workshops.

items.text: The Private Wealth Advisor Program offers education, training, and accreditation plus enhanced capabilities and product solutions.
items.quote: our Private Wealth Advisor Program offers education, training, and accreditation along with enhanced capabilities and product solutions.

items.text: About 370 advisors had completed or were enrolled in the Private Wealth Advisor Program as of the fiscal third quarter 2025.
items.quote: About 370 advisors, have completed or are enrolled in our Private Wealth Advisor Program

items.text: Raymond James has invested in transition teams to provide seamless onboarding transitions for newly affiliated advisors.
items.quote: we have invested in the transition teams as well, given them more capabilities and capacities to really help with the uptake to ensure that we have seamless transitions of the new advisors

items.text: The Private Wealth Advisor designation program (launched September 2022) provides training, coaching, and a peer network for advisors specializing in high-net-worth clients; nearly 450 advisors had earned the designation as of September 2026.
items.quote: the firm's Raymond James Private Wealth Advisor designation program, launched in September 2022, which provides training, coaching, and a peer network for advisors who specialize in high-net-worth clients... As of September 2026, nearly 450 advisors have earned the designation

a3.RJF.reason: Passages describe onboarding/training programs for new and trainee advisors, including Wealth Management Associate, Advisor Mastery, Private Wealth Advisor, and transition teams.

a4.RJF.label: fact

items.quote: The number of financial advisors as of September 30, 2025 increased compared to the prior year, as new recruits and trainees that were moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements.

items.quote: Raymond James no longer reports advisor headcount, but it had about 8,900 advisors the last time headcount was officially broken out.

a5.RJF.label: fact

items.text: As a retention tool, Raymond James may grant equity awards under various retention programs and offers non-qualified deferred compensation plans that serve as a retention tool.
items.quote: As an additional retention tool, we may grant equity awards in connection with initial employment or under various retention programs... we also offer various non-qualified deferred compensation plans that provide a return to the participant, as well as a retention tool to the firm.

items.text: In fiscal 2025, adjusted compensation expense included amortization of retention awards to existing advisors (along with transition assistance to recruited advisors) of $355 million in aggregate, up about 11% from fiscal 2024.
items.quote: In fiscal year 2025, adjusted compensation expense included the amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors in the aggregate amount of $355 million, representing an increase of approximately 11% compared to fiscal 2024.

items.text: PCG recruiting and retention-related compensation includes cash and equity awards issued for recruiting, as retention for existing advisors, or in acquisitions, expensed over typically 5 to 10 years.
items.quote: PCG recruiting and retention-related compensation includes expenses related to cash and equity awards issued in conjunction with recruiting activities, as retention for existing advisors, or in conjunction with our acquisitions... Such awards are expensed over the requisite service period (typically between 5 and 10 years).
items.definition: cash and equity awards issued in conjunction with recruiting activities, as retention for existing advisors, or in conjunction with acquisitions

items.text: RSU awards may be granted under retention programs and are generally restricted for three to five years.
items.quote: We may grant RSU awards under the Plan in connection with initial employment or under various retention programs... Under the Plan, RSU awards are generally restricted for a three - to five-year period.

items.text: Retirement and deferred compensation arrangements include an employee stock ownership plan, profit-sharing plan, 401(k) matching, an employee stock purchase plan, and a non-qualified deferred compensation LTIP.
items.quote: we make annual contributions to support the retirement goals of each associate through our employee stock ownership plan and our profit-sharing plan... Our LTIP is a non-qualified deferred compensation plan that provides benefits to certain employees who meet certain compensation or production requirements.

items.text: Raymond James uses tiered payout systems, so as advisor production increases advisors move higher up the payout grid.
items.quote: even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems. And so as production increases, you kind of get higher up on the payout grid as well.

a5.RJF.reason: Passages describe retention awards, deferred compensation, RSU retention programs, retirement plans, and tiered payout compensation arrangements for advisors.

a6.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James mitigates advisor departure risk through financial advisor succession planning and by providing advisors resources to support their practices.
items.quote: We seek to mitigate these risks through financial advisor succession planning and by providing our financial advisors with a broad range of services and resources to support their practices.

items.text: With planned retirements, assets are generally retained at the firm pursuant to advisor succession plans.
items.quote: Generally, with planned retirements, assets are retained at the firm pursuant to advisor succession plans.

items.text: For independent advisors, the firm offers succession and acquisition guidance to make career-critical decisions.
items.quote: Succession and acquisition: Make career-critical decisions with specialized guidance

items.text: For RIA custody clients, Raymond James offers succession planning and acquisition support with a team of specialists.
items.quote: Succession Planning and Aquisition: Everything you need to plan for your next step and a team of specialists to guide you

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab's CEO says the firm built its advisor business around helping independent advisors grow, compete and succeed, with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support.
items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed. Today, we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says the advisor business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service, and the breadth to support advisors as their businesses and clients' needs become more complex, and that is why Schwab wins.
items.quote: This business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service and the breadth to support advisers as their businesses and their clients' needs become more complex. That is why we win.

items.text: Schwab's Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.
items.quote: The Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent registered investment advisors (RIAs), independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says it is hard for other firms to compete with Schwab's size, scale, and the breadth and strength of its capabilities in Advisor Services, including the custody offering, consulting and advice, and support for advisors' drive to independence.
items.quote: it's hard for other firms to compete with our size, scale, and the breadth and strength of our capabilities, whether it's the custody offering... the consulting and advice and expertise that we bring, the support we bring to help them in their drive to independence.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says the firm is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs, including lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.
items.quote: we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs. We've grown our lending support, alternatives capability, and expanded our institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform...

items.text: Schwab describes itself as the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
items.quote: The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service

items.text: Schwab's CEO says independent advisors win in the marketplace because the fiduciary model works and there is a bull market for advice and convenience, and that as advisors win and Schwab supports their growth, Schwab wins as well.
items.quote: the advisers continue to win in the marketplace because the fiduciary model works, because there's a bull market for advice and convenience and the independent advisers have a great model. And so as they win and we're successful in supporting their growth, we win as well.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says that in advisor services the firm is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.
items.quote: In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says the firm launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.
items.quote: we launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says the firm wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, and is increasingly trying to play the role of being the advisors' bank.
items.quote: Schwab wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending , private market investing, and long-short investment strategies... 'We are increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank and helping them manage both sides of the balance sheet for their clients.'

items.text: Schwab's CEO says the firm's job and role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps advisors support their clients and helps their firm thrive, not to tell advisors what they should become or how big they should be.
items.quote: Our job is not to tell you what you should become, how big you should be or what success looks like for you... Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive.

items.text: Schwab's CEO says the firm has tried to make the path to independence as easy as possible by investing in its own process and working with partners to have a great experience ready for advisors and make the transition easy.
items.quote: We've tried to make the path to independence as easy as possible... We work with partners like we did with Open Arc. We work with Dynasty … collectively, we try to have a great experience ready for them, and try to make the transition easy once they decide they want to be independent.

items.text: Schwab's CFO says Schwab provides an industry-leading value proposition to individual investors and RIAs, and has created an exceptional offering that is highly trusted and valued by individual investors and RIAs.
items.quote: Schwab provides an industry-leading value proposition to individual investors and RIAs... We have created an exceptional offering in the marketplace that is highly trusted and valued by individual investors and RIAs

items.text: Schwab's CEO says Schwab remains the trusted platform of choice for investors and registered investment advisers and is #1 by RIA custodial assets.
items.quote: We remain the trusted platform of choice for investors and registered investment advisers. We are #1 by total client assets, #1 by RIA custodial assets and #1 in daily average trades.

a1.SCHW.reason: The passages contain multiple direct statements by Schwab executives and documents describing Schwab's value proposition to independent advisors.

a2.SCHW.label: not_found
a2.SCHW.reason: None of the provided passages compares Schwab's and Raymond James's value propositions to independent advisors; they discuss only Schwab.

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James describes its value proposition to advisors as 'best of both worlds': a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions that resonates across all of its affiliation options.
items.quote: Our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options.

items.text: RJF says its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.
items.quote: our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: Raymond James's independent advisor page describes affiliation as 'a partnership in independence,' with independent contractors getting the support of a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer.
items.quote: A partnership in independence... Enjoy the rewards of running your own practice with the support of a full-service, self-clearing New York Stock Exchange-member broker/dealer.

items.text: Raymond James says AdvisorChoice lets advisors match their professional goals to the right affiliation option, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility, backed by a leading independent financial firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: The firm attributes its ability to attract high-quality advisors to its values-based culture, commitment to service, and the unique ways it provides services to financial advisors.
items.quote: Our ability to attract high quality advisors is based on our values-based culture, our commitment to service, and the unique ways in which we provide services to our financial advisors.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry describes the value proposition as having the largest addressable market across affiliation options (employee, independent contractor, RIA custody) with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them. It's not a new venture for us.

items.text: Raymond James says advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities: it offers a unique combination of an adviser- and client-focused culture with leading technologies, products and solutions.
items.quote: At Raymond James, advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture together with leading technologies, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: For independent RIAs, Raymond James describes 'the best of both worlds': complete freedom and control over the business with the robust support of a premier financial services firm.
items.quote: you'll have complete freedom and control to do what's best for both, along with the robust support of a premier financial services firm.

items.text: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options under the name AdvisorChoice.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®.

a1.RJF.reason: The passages state Raymond James's own descriptions of its value proposition to independent advisors, so these are facts.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James contrasts its 'powerfully personal' value proposition with 'other firms' that talk about IRRs and exit periods in three to five years; RJF focuses instead on personal relationships with financial advisors and their clients.
items.quote: other firms are talking about IRRs and exit periods in three to five years, or funnels and all sorts of impersonal things. What we're doing in that world... is really doubling and tripling down on what we've always done, which is really focusing on the personal relationships with financial advisors

items.text: Shoukry says Raymond James does not lead with the highest check but leads with culture and capabilities, which it calls a true differentiated value proposition.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check... we lead with culture and capabilities. And so we have a true differentiated value proposition.

items.text: Shoukry says many competitors that also focus on personal relationships and have similar cultures invest a fraction of Raymond James's technology spend, while RJF's long-term focus and personal relationships differentiate it.
items.quote: a lot of our competitors who also are focused on personal relationships, and that have similar cultures, their technology investment, for example, is a fraction of ours.

items.text: Raymond James says its AI/technology investments are ones smaller regional firms and many independent firms can't afford, and PE-backed firms won't make because of multi-year payback periods and short exit horizons.
items.quote: These are investments that the smaller regional firms and a lot of the independent firms can't afford to make. Some of the PE-backed firms aren't willing to make that long-term investment because these are payback periods of multiple years.

items.text: In Canada, RJF says its 'best of both worlds' value proposition is similar to the U.S.: a more advisor-centric culture plus all the capabilities advisors coming from the big six banks are used to.
items.quote: We offer a more advisor-centric culture and all the capabilities that the advisors, that most of them come from those banks have become accustomed to having.

items.text: RJF describes its differentiated value proposition as advisers not having to choose between culture and capabilities—an adviser- and client-focused culture plus leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: RJF says its client-first culture, robust technology and product platforms and strong balance sheet continue to differentiate it as a destination of choice for advisers.
items.quote: Our client-first culture, together with our robust technology and product platforms and strong balance sheet, continues to differentiate Raymond James as a destination of choice for financial advisers across our affiliation options.

items.text: RJF says having the culture, products, platform and technology is differentiating it more than ever.
items.quote: having the culture and the products and the platform and the technology is really differentiating us more than ever.

a2.RJF.reason: The passages contain Raymond James's own contrastive statements about how its value proposition differs from competitors, which is the RJF-side evidence for the comparison.

Merrill: The 2025 Form 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets, and that Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, provides comprehensive wealth management solutions targeted to high net worth and ultra high net worth clients. In its November 5, 2025 investor-day deck, Merrill | Private Bank describes its approach as "Serving the wealth continuum of clients," and the firm says the Wealth Continuum allows it to deliver as one company, is its engine for lasting growth, and gives it the capabilities to deliver for every client in the way they want to be served.

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Written definition: a count with no written definition at Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('Financial advisors (actual)', EDJ-10K-2025#130); publishes no count of this metric; reports a related figure instead at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('perform investment advisory functions (including research)? 4127', SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1); stated by Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('Includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Independent contractor advisors: not stated by Morgan Stanley, Merrill (Bank of America Corporation); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('Through the Advisor Services segment, Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients', SCHW-10K-2025#23); stated by Edward Jones ('The Partnership’s financial advisors are employees or partners of the Partnership.', EDJ-10K-2025#35); counted by Raymond James Financial ('Independent contractors 5,065', RJF-10K-2025#227).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Business lines in the count: counted by Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('two operating and reportable segments based upon geographic location, the U.S. and Canada', EDJ-10K-2025#145), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation; excluded by Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Date of the registered count: dated for Morgan Stanley (2020-12-31, 'Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones (2025-12-31, 'At year end 20,425', EDJ-10K-2025#130), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) (2023-12-31, 'Total wealth advisors (3) 18,916', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial (2025-09-30, 'Total advisors 8,943', RJF-10K-2025#227); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation.

Morgan Stanley - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2020-12-31 (MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (MS-SUPP-2025Q4, MS-SUPP-2026Q1, MS-SUPP-2026Q2, MS-SUPP-2026Q3).

Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2023-12-31 (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (BAC-SUPP-2025Q4, BAC-SUPP-2026Q1, BAC-SUPP-2026Q2, BAC-SUPP-2026Q3).
GWIM is not Merrill: the segment also includes Bank of America Private Bank.

(BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); business lines in the count: 'all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking' (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); not stated: independent contractor advisors, trainees | Raymond James Financial: 'Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.' (RJF-10K-2025#228); independent contractor advisors: 'Independent contractors 5,065' (RJF-10K-2025#227); excludes: 'Advisors in our RCS division are not included' (RJF-10K-2025#228); not stated: trainees.

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Written definition: a count with no written definition at Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('Financial advisors (actual)', EDJ-10K-2025#130); publishes no count of this metric; reports a related figure instead at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('perform investment advisory functions (including research)? 4127', SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1); stated by Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('Includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Independent contractor advisors: not stated by Morgan Stanley, Merrill (Bank of America Corporation); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation ('Through the Advisor Services segment, Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients', SCHW-10K-2025#23); stated by Edward Jones ('The Partnership’s financial advisors are employees or partners of the Partnership.', EDJ-10K-2025#35); counted by Raymond James Financial ('Independent contractors 5,065', RJF-10K-2025#227).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Business lines in the count: counted by Morgan Stanley ('Wealth Management representatives', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones ('two operating and reportable segments based upon geographic location, the U.S. and Canada', EDJ-10K-2025#145), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) ('all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation; excluded by Raymond James Financial ('Advisors in our RCS division are not included', RJF-10K-2025#228).

Advisor headcount, how the definitions differ - Date of the registered count: dated for Morgan Stanley (2020-12-31, 'Wealth Management representatives 15,950', MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), Edward Jones (2025-12-31, 'At year end 20,425', EDJ-10K-2025#130), Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) (2023-12-31, 'Total wealth advisors (3) 18,916', BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), Raymond James Financial (2025-09-30, 'Total advisors 8,943', RJF-10K-2025#227); no advisor count at The Charles Schwab Corporation.

Morgan Stanley - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2020-12-31 (MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (MS-SUPP-2025Q4, MS-SUPP-2026Q1, MS-SUPP-2026Q2, MS-SUPP-2026Q3).

Merrill (Bank of America Corporation) - Advisor headcount: latest count found in the quarterly financial supplements: 2023-12-31 (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2); no count found in the quarterly financial supplements read since (BAC-SUPP-2025Q4, BAC-SUPP-2026Q1, BAC-SUPP-2026Q2, BAC-SUPP-2026Q3).
GWIM is not Merrill: the segment also includes Bank of America Private Bank.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that as one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., it is able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients and harness resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs.
items.quote: As one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., we are able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, and harness the resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs.

items.text: Schwab says coupled with scale, its operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across businesses creates a cost advantage that enables competitive pricing while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels.
items.quote: Coupled with scale, our operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables us to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels.

items.text: Schwab lists its brand and corporate reputation as a competitive advantage that enables it to attract clients and employees while credibly introducing new products.
items.quote: Schwab's reputation and brand across multiple constituents enable us to attract clients and employees while credibly introducing new products to the market.

items.text: Schwab's service culture earns client trust and loyalty and increases the likelihood that clients will refer others.
items.quote: Delivering a great client experience earns the trust and loyalty of clients and increases the likelihood that those clients will refer others.

items.text: Schwab says its scale combined with expense discipline decreased its cost per account 20% over the last five years while keeping it the industry leader on expense on client assets (EOCA).
items.quote: Our scale, combined with our expense discipline, has allowed us to decrease our cost per account 20% over the last five years while driving our ability to remain the industry leader as measured by expense on client assets, or EOCA
items.unit: decrease in cost per account over five years

items.text: Schwab says its cost per account continues to decrease and its expense on client assets is the lowest in the industry, with scale powering reinvestment capacity and durable earnings power.
items.quote: Our cost per account continues to decrease, and our expense on client assets is the lowest in the industry.

a1.SCHW.reason: Passages state Schwab's scale, efficiency, brand, and service advantages and how they support attracting clients.

a2.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab says its sheer scale combined with efficiency efforts keeps its cost-to-serve clients low, which allows it to invest in client capabilities that fuel growth.
items.quote: our sheer scale, combined with efficiency efforts that make it easier for clients to do business with us, keeps our cost-to-serve clients low. This also allows us to invest in client capabilities that will fuel our growth

items.text: Schwab couples its scale and resources with expense discipline to keep costs low and ensure products and solutions are affordable and responsive to client needs.
items.quote: management works to couple Schwab's scale and resources with ongoing expense discipline to keep costs low and ensure that products and solutions are affordable as well as responsive to client needs.

items.text: Schwab's scale and efficiency efforts keep its cost-to-serve clients low so it can reinvest in new capabilities and experiences to serve clients' evolving needs.
items.quote: our scale and efficiency efforts will not only help us keep our cost-to-serve clients low so we can reinvest in new capabilities and experiences to serve their evolving needs

items.text: Schwab uses scale and efficiency initiatives to operate more efficiently, maintain low cost to serve, and reinvest in growth initiatives.
items.quote: these are initiatives that benefit clients while allowing us to operate more efficiently, maintain our low cost to serve, and reinvest in our growth initiatives.

items.text: Schwab says its ability to execute at scale drives efficiencies that allow it to reinvest in growth.
items.quote: Our ability to execute at scale continues to drive efficiencies that allow us to reinvest in growth.

items.text: Schwab's spending plan supports new client growth through investments in branches, financial consultants, and advertising and marketing while harnessing incremental scale and efficiency.
items.quote: driving new client growth and deepening relationships with individual investors and RIAs by further expanding our leading suite of offerings to serve their evolving needs, bolstering our best-in-class service experience while also harnessing incremental scale and efficiency

a2.SCHW.reason: Passages describe how Schwab uses scale and efficiency to keep cost-to-serve low and reinvest in growth and client acquisition.

a3.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab serves and acquires clients through financial consultants in branches, service professionals answering phones, advisor services relationship managers, and digital channels.
items.quote: through the financial consultants in our branches, through our service professionals answering the phones, through our advisor services, relationship managers, and through our digital channels when that's how our clients want to engage.

items.text: Schwab invests in marketing spend, which drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients.
items.quote: We are investing in our marketing spend, which drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients.
items.unit: of new-to-firm retail clients driven by marketing spend

items.text: In 2025 Schwab opened 10 new branches and hired hundreds of financial consultants and wealth advisors to support client growth.
items.quote: We opened 10 new branches and hired hundreds of financial consultants and wealth advisors.

items.text: Schwab invests in more branches, more financial consultants, strategic marketing and advertising (including adapting to LLMs), an RIA support ecosystem, and bringing Schwab to workplace clients.
items.quote: more branches in local communities, more financial consultants, strategic marketing and advertising, including adapting our marketing to the increased influence of LLMs, the build-out of an RIA support ecosystem, and investments in bringing the breadth of Schwab to our workplace clients.

items.text: Schwab uses answer engine optimization in marketing to appear on AI platforms where investors do research.
items.quote: We're already reaching a growing number of clients through the answer engine optimization work that our marketing team is doing to ensure we show up on the AI platforms where investors return.

items.text: Schwab launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.
items.quote: we launched Advisor ProDirect, a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.

items.text: About half of new-to-firm retail clients initiated access to Schwab's thinkorswim trading platform in 2025.
items.quote: about half of new-to-firm retail clients initiated access to our industry-leading thinkorswim platform.
items.unit: of new-to-firm retail clients initiating thinkorswim access

items.text: Schwab uses golf sponsorships and related content (Charles Schwab Challenge, documentary series, Invested in the Game podcast, branded streaming integrations) to connect with investors around a shared passion.
items.quote: Golf creates meaningful moments for Schwab to connect with investors around a shared passion

items.text: Schwab serves clients through about 400 branches in local communities in the U.S. and overseas.
items.quote: thousands of interactions in our 400 branches in local communities across our country and overseas.

a3.SCHW.reason: Passages name Schwab's client acquisition channels and tactics, including branches, advisors, digital, marketing, and sponsorships.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has an exclusive partnership with Carta under which Carta will refer private stock plan companies to Morgan Stanley as they move into going public, and the firm is committed to making it a seamless experience for those clients.
items.quote: we have an exclusive partnership with Carta, which means that they will refer those private different stock plans or different corporate companies to Morgan Stanley as they move into going public.

items.text: Morgan Stanley at Work, with its exclusive Carta partnership, positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies, giving it early relationships as workplace companies grow.
items.quote: Our Morgan Stanley at Work business, with its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions us as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies.

items.text: The firm first retains workplace assets when they vest, and then, through technology and investment, those workplace assets migrate to the advisor-led channel as they seek advice.
items.quote: we are seeing channel migration, and that's with technology and investment, where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice

items.text: As IPOs come to market, workplace participants bring their assets to Morgan Stanley, dropping them into self-directed accounts and also moving them directly into advisor-led accounts.

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James's AdvisorChoice® affiliation options are Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA.
items.quote: Traditional Employee: Get everything you expect from working for a firm with a powerful difference – book ownership. Advisor Select: Lead your own branch... Independent Contractor: Operate as an independent financial advisor... Bank & Credit Union: Leverage national strength... Corporate RIA: Exercise true autonomy...

items.text: The affiliation spectrum also includes an RIA & Custody Services option offering strategic, financial and administrative control of a practice.
items.quote: RIA & Custody Services: Take strategic, financial and administrative control of your practice with a full-service partner at the ready.

items.text: An investor-day graphic lists the AdvisorChoice spectrum as Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services.
items.quote: EMPLOYEE ADVISOR (RJA) ... ADVISOR SELECT ... INDEPENDENT ADVISOR (ICD) ... BANKS AND CREDIT UNIONS ... IAR* (CORPORATE RIA) ... RIA** & CUSTODY SERVICES

items.text: The 10-K states financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services division.
items.quote: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.

a1.RJF.reason: The passages explicitly list the affiliation options offered under AdvisorChoice.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: For the Traditional Employee model, the payout is up to 50% plus a full array of competitive employee benefits; compliance support comes from the branch manager and home office.
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee ... Payout + Benefits: Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings. Compliance: Compliance support will be provided to you by your branch manager and the home office.

items.text: The Advisor Select model offers a 70-80% gross payout and a full array of competitive employee benefits.
items.quote: Model: Advisor Select ... Payout + Benefits: 70-80% gross payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: The Independent Contractor model offers an 81% to 90% payout and benefits created through third-party partnerships.
items.quote: Model: Independent Contractor ... Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: Bank & Credit Union advisors receive a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.
items.quote: Model: Bank & Credit Union ... Payout + Benefits: Get the support you need during your transition by receiving a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.

items.text: The Corporate RIA model offers an 81% to 90% payout and benefits created through third-party partnerships.
items.quote: Model: Corporate RIA ... Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third-party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: RIA & Custody Services advisors work with their RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation and create their own benefits package.
items.quote: Model: RIA & Custody Services ... Payout + Benefits: Work with your RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation. Create your own benefits package.

items.text: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and therefore receive a higher payout percentage than employee financial advisors.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.

items.text: Employee financial advisors' compensation primarily includes a payout on the revenues they generate and participation in the firm's employee benefit plans.
items.quote: Compensation for these financial advisors primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate and such advisors also participate in the firm’s employee benefit plans.

items.text: Management says independent payouts are higher because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, and the employee channel has tiered payout systems.
items.quote: the independent payouts are higher because they cover their overhead costs, their real estate, their health insurance, et cetera... even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems. And so as production increases, you kind of get higher up on the payout grid as well.

a2.RJF.reason: The passages state payouts, benefits and cost responsibilities for each affiliation option.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Growth in RIA & Custody Services client assets is partly due to financial advisors transferring into RCS from the firm's other advisor channels; the firm expects continued transfers but does not expect them to significantly affect results.
items.quote: The growth in RCS client assets over time is partially due to transfers into RCS from our other financial advisor channels. We may continue to experience transfers to our RCS division; however, consistent with our experience in recent fiscal years, we would not expect these financial advisor transfers to significantly impact our results of operations.

items.text: Advisors who moved to the RIA model have largely moved to Raymond James's own RIA, so the firm has kept the assets.
items.quote: The biggest movement of people that have gone to RIA, fortunately, have gone to our RIA, so we've kept the assets.

items.text: The firm participates in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take and their ability to solicit clients when they affiliate with a new firm.
items.quote: We participate, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting (“Protocol”), a voluntary agreement among many firms in the industry that governs, among other things, the client information that financial advisors may take with them when they affiliate with a new firm and the financial advisor’s ability to solicit clients of their prior firm.

items.text: The 10-K describes an industry-wide trend of advisors departing traditional firms to form independent RIAs or join existing third-party RIAs, some backed by private equity.
items.quote: financial advisors are departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs, some of which are backed by private equity investors.

a3.RJF.reason: The passages describe transfers into RCS, the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, and related departure dynamics.

a4.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Management describes the model as AdvisorChoice®—a platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that’s right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility... AdvisorChoice® A platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them.

items.text: Management says Raymond James has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an advisor could want and is agnostic about how advisors affiliate.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James... how you affiliate with us, we're indifferent to.

claims.text: Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of April 21, 2026) lists the AdvisorChoice® affiliation options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA, describing Traditional Employee as offering book ownership, Advisor Select as leading one's own branch, Independent Contractor as operating as an independent financial advisor, Bank & Credit Union as leveraging national strength, and Corporate RIA as exercising true autonomy.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The same recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states the affiliation spectrum also includes an RIA & Custody Services option, described as 'Take strategic, financial and administrative control of your practice with a full-service partner at the ready.'
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: A graphic in the investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) lists the AdvisorChoice spectrum as Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) states that financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

For the Traditional Employee option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states a payout of up to 50% plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, with compliance support provided by the branch manager and the home office.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: For the Advisor Select option, the same page (content as of April 21, 2026) states a 70-80% gross payout and a full array of competitive employee benefits.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: For the Independent Contractor option, the same page (content as of April 21, 2026) states an 81% to 90% payout, with benefits created through third-party partnerships.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: For the Bank & Credit Union option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states advisors receive a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: For the Corporate RIA option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states an 81% to 90% payout, with benefits created through third-party partnerships.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: For the RIA & Custody Services option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states advisors work with their RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation and create their own benefits package.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) states that compensation for employee financial advisors primarily includes a payout on the revenues they generate, and that such advisors also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (published April 22, 2026), management explained that independent payouts are higher because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, such as real estate and health insurance, and that even the employee side has tiered payout systems where advisors move higher on the payout grid as production increases.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) states that Raymond James participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, a voluntary agreement among many firms that governs the client information financial advisors may take with them when they affiliate with a new firm and their ability to solicit clients of their prior firm.

The same 10-K describes an industry-wide trend in which financial advisors are departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs, some of which are backed by private equity investors.

The recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) describes AdvisorChoice® as a platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them, letting advisors match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, with each option offering a unique combination of support, freedom, and flexibility.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said Raymond James has the largest addressable market in the industry because it has all the affiliation options an advisor could want and is agnostic—indifferent—about how advisors affiliate with the firm.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 (published July 23, 2025), management described the value proposition as 'best of both worlds'—an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions—and said it continues to resonate with advisors across all affiliation options.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), management said the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (published April 22, 2026), management stated its focus is to remain the absolute best destination for financial advisers and their clients across all of its affiliation options.
On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said growth remains focused on quality over quantity.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said recruiting is not something that can be turned on and off quarter to quarter, and requires consistency in retaining existing advisers, recruiting new advisers, and having the team focused on finding advisers who are good cultural fits with the firm across its affiliation options.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), management said recruited advisors come from competitor types including wires, regionals, and other independents, and described those firms as friendly competitors who are doing good jobs keeping their advisors.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 (published July 23, 2025), management identified private equity-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel competitive dynamic in advisor recruiting, saying they have been extremely aggressive in trading and paying at higher and higher multiples over the last three years in particular.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) names its direct competitors as other national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers, and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and notes competition from more recent entrants including fintechs.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended September 30, 2024 (published October 23, 2024), management said a couple of OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division had decided to leave the platform, and roughly $3 billion of AUA left the firm in the fiscal fourth quarter.
On the same call, the firm anticipated approximately $5 billion of assets associated with those departing OSJ firms would complete their transfers off the platform in early fiscal 2025.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 (published October 22, 2025), management said the firm would lose a platform through bank M&A the next quarter, approximately $2.7 billion of assets.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended December 31, 2024 (published January 29, 2025), management said the large departure previously discussed had essentially almost totally gone from the platform, and that it does not see anything big on the leaving side, though there is always some attrition.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) warns that financial advisors may leave the firm, including for independent RIAs or third-party RIAs, and that retiring financial advisors without a successor affiliated with the firm may sell their practices to unaffiliated third parties, which could negatively affect AUA.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that the drivers of continued expanded Wealth Management margins are twofold: building fee-based revenues and fee-based assets by introducing clients to the advice-based (advisor-led) model, while self-directed clients generate increasing transactional revenues through investments in E*TRADE.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab's largest sources of net revenues are net interest revenue, asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees, supported by the combination of its broker-dealer, bank, and asset management operating subsidiaries.
items.quote: Schwab's largest sources of net revenues are net interest revenue, asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees. These revenue streams are supported by the combination of our broker-dealer, bank, and asset management operating subsidiaries, each of which brings specific capabilities that enable us to provide clients with the products and services they are seeking.

items.text: Net interest revenue is the difference between interest generated on interest-earning assets and interest paid on funding sources; Schwab's primary funding source for interest-earning assets is uninvested client cash balances held on its balance sheet, and its interest-earning assets are primarily high-quality fixed income securities, margin loans, and bank loans.
items.quote: Net interest revenue is the difference between interest generated on interest-earning assets and interest paid on funding sources. Schwab's primary funding source for interest-earning assets is uninvested client cash balances held on our balance sheet as part of our clients' overall relationship with the Company. Schwab's interest-earning assets are primarily comprised of high-quality fixed income securities, margin loans, and bank loans.

items.text: Asset management and administration fees are primarily earned from proprietary money market mutual funds, proprietary and third-party mutual funds and ETFs, and fee-based managed investing solutions.
items.quote: Asset management and administration fees are primarily earned from proprietary money market mutual funds, proprietary and third-party mutual funds and ETFs, and fee-based managed investing solutions.

items.text: Trading revenue includes commissions earned for executing trades for clients in certain individual equities, options, futures, fixed income securities, and certain third-party mutual funds and ETFs; order flow revenue; and principal transactions revenue earned primarily from actions to support client trading in fixed income securities.
items.quote: Trading revenue includes commissions earned for executing trades for clients in certain individual equities, options, futures, fixed income securities, and certain third-party mutual funds and ETFs; order flow revenue; and principal transactions revenue earned primarily from actions to support client trading in fixed income securities.

items.quote: In Q2 2026, Schwab generated nearly $3.4 billion in net interest revenue, largely on approximately $485.7 billion held in sweep accounts.

items.text: Schwab's bank deposit account fees increased in the second quarter of 2026 primarily due to improved net yields, partially offset by lower average bank deposit account balances.
items.quote: Bank deposit account fees increased for both segments primarily due to improved net yields partially offset by lower average BDA balances.

a1.SCHW.reason: The passages state Schwab's revenue streams and the mechanisms by which its brokerage and bank earn on client assets, so these are facts.

a3.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Wealth managers earn revenue on client cash by investing or lending uninvested balances at yields higher than the rates they pay clients; when interest rates climb, yields on loans, floating-rate assets, and reinvested fixed-income securities rise, widening the spread that drives net interest income.
items.quote: Wealth managers earn revenue on client cash by investing or lending uninvested balances at yields higher than the rates they pay clients. When interest rates climb, so do yields on loans, floating-rate assets, and reinvested fixed-income securities, widening the spread that drives net interest income.

items.text: Fitch said firms with greater exposure to floating-rate assets, faster reinvestment of maturing holdings, and less reliance on rate-sensitive funding are better positioned to see more immediate net interest income gains.
items.quote: Fitch said firms with greater exposure to floating-rate assets, faster reinvestment of maturing holdings, and less reliance on rate-sensitive funding are better positioned to see more immediate net interest income gains.

items.text: Raymond James, which holds primarily floating-rate securities and corporate loans alongside certain variable-rate sweep fee arrangements with third-party banks, is positioned to see more immediate earnings benefits when rates rise because its repricing happens faster in response to short-term rate movements.
items.quote: Raymond James, which holds primarily floating-rate securities and corporate loans alongside certain variable-rate sweep fee arrangements with third-party banks, is positioned to see more immediate earnings benefits when rates rise - its repricing happens faster in response to short-term rate movements.

items.text: LPL, which does not operate its own bank and instead places client deposits with partner institutions that pay it a fee, holds roughly 40% of insured cash account balances under variable-rate agreements as of the second quarter of 2026, so a portion of its earnings reprices relatively quickly while the fixed-rate segment lags.
items.quote: LPL, which does not operate its own bank and instead places client deposits with partner institutions that pay it a fee, holds roughly 40% of insured cash account balances under variable-rate agreements as of the second quarter of 2026, according to Fitch.
items.unit: of insured cash account balances under variable-rate agreements

items.text: Ameriprise's bank investment portfolio, with a 4.2-year duration and 6% in floating-rate securities, is weighted toward fixed-rate assets, meaning repricing would be more gradual.
items.quote: Ameriprise's bank investment portfolio, with a 4.2-year duration and 6% in floating-rate securities, is weighted toward fixed-rate assets, meaning repricing would be more gradual.

items.text: Stifel's commercial, fund-banking and venture deposit mix makes it harder to isolate the revenue contribution from sweep balances specifically, according to Fitch.
items.quote: Stifel's commercial, fund-banking and venture deposit mix makes it harder to isolate the revenue contribution from sweep balances specifically, Fitch noted.

items.text: Schwab's CEO said return on client assets (ROCA) for Managed Investing solutions is two times that of retail, which diversifies the firm's revenue streams.
items.quote: At the same time, return on client assets, or ROCA, for Managed Investing solutions is two times that of retail, which diversifies our revenue streams as we delight clients.

items.text: Schwab's Investor Services segment provides retail brokerage, investment advisory, and banking and trust services to individual investors, and retirement plan and business services, as well as other corporate brokerage services, to businesses and their employees.
items.quote: The Investor Services segment provides retail brokerage, investment advisory, and banking and trust services to individual investors, and retirement plan and business services, as well as other corporate brokerage services, to businesses and their employees.

items.text: Schwab's Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers; revenues and expenses are attributed to the two segments based on which segment services the client.
items.quote: The Advisor Services segment provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers. Revenues and expenses are attributed to the two segments based on which segment services the client.

a3.SCHW.reason: The passages state the cash spread model, the firm-specific drivers of differences in cash earnings, and how advisor-led models earn, so they are facts for the comparison.

a2.EDJ.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones states that it primarily derives revenues from fees for providing investment advisory and other account services to clients, fees for assets held by clients, and commissions for distributing mutual fund shares and insurance products and for securities transactions.
items.quote: primarily derives revenues from fees for providing investment advisory and other account services to its clients, fees for assets held by clients and commissions for the distribution of mutual fund shares and insurance products and the purchase or sale of securities

items.text: Within fee revenue, Edward Jones's asset-based fees include advisory program fees based on the average daily market value of client assets in the program and contractual rates, and these fees are affected by changes in market values and by client dollars invested in and divested from the accounts.
items.quote: fee revenue is composed of asset-based fees and account and activity fees. Asset-based fees include advisory program fees which are based on the average daily market value of client assets in the program, as well as contractual rates.

items.text: Edward Jones earns revenue on clients' assets through service fees and revenue sharing received under agreements with certain mutual fund and insurance companies.
items.quote: The Partnership earns revenue on clients’ assets through service fees and revenue sharing received under agreements with certain mutual fund and insurance companies.

items.text: For mutual funds, Edward Jones's service fees are generally based on the average daily market value of client assets held in a company's mutual fund or insurance product, and service fee revenue is recognized monthly once the transaction price is known and the services have been performed.
items.quote: Service fees are generally based on the average daily market value of client assets held in a company's mutual fund or insurance product. ... service fee revenue is recognized monthly at the time the market constraints have been removed, the transaction price is known and the services have been performed.

items.text: Edward Jones's other asset-based fee revenue consists of revenue sharing, fund adviser fees, cash solutions and Trust Co. fees.
items.quote: Other asset-based fee revenue consists of revenue sharing, fund adviser fees, cash solutions and Trust Co. fees.

items.text: Edward Jones also earns certain asset-based fees and per-account fees from the Edward Jones Money Market Fund, some or all of which may be voluntarily waived, while its subsidiary Olive Street earns investment management fees as the fund's investment adviser.
items.quote: Olive Street is the investment adviser of the Money Market Fund and earns investment management fees as the investment adviser to the Money Market Fund. Edward Jones also earns certain asset-based fees and per-account fees from the Money Market Fund, some or all of which may be voluntarily waived.

items.text: In addition to advisory programs, Edward Jones earns asset-based fees from trust services and investment management services offered through Edward Jones Trust Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary.
items.quote: the Partnership earns asset-based fees from the trust services and investment management services offered to its clients through Edward Jones Trust Company (“Trust Co.”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of JFC.

a2.EDJ.reason: The passages state how Edward Jones's advisor-led model earns asset-based fee revenue from advisory programs, service fees, revenue sharing, cash solutions, money market fund fees and trust services.

a2.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill's CFO stated that the wealth management business is primarily a fee-based advice-driven model, with about 30 percent of revenue coming from net interest income derived from GWIM clients and their loan and deposit balances.
items.quote: While this is primarily a fee-based advice-driven model, about 30% of our revenue is now net interest income derived from GWIM clients and the large loan and deposit balances on us.

items.text: In the fourth quarter of 2024, Merrill's CFO stated that about 30 percent of GWIM revenue remained in net interest income, which complements the fees earned in the advice model.
items.quote: Importantly, about 30% of our revenue remains in net interest income, which complements the fees earned in our advice model, and those have also grown.

items.text: In 2025, GWIM asset management fees increased 12 percent to $15.4 billion, reflecting higher market valuations and positive AUM flows, while higher brokerage fees reflected increased transactional volume.
items.quote: The increase was primarily driven by higher asset management fees, which increased 12 percent to $15.4 billion, reflecting higher market valuations and the impact of positive AUM flows as well as higher brokerage fees due to increased transactional volume, partially offset by the impact of lower AUM pricing.

items.text: In 2025, GWIM noninterest income, which primarily includes investment and brokerage services income, increased $1.7 billion to $17.7 billion.
items.quote: Noninterest income, which primarily includes investment and brokerage services income, increased $1.7 billion to $17.7 billion.

items.text: In 2025, Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $20.7 billion increased nine percent, primarily driven by higher asset management fees and higher brokerage fees from increased transactional volume.
items.quote: Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $20.7 billion increased nine percent primarily driven by higher asset management fees reflecting higher market valuations and the impact of positive AUM flows, as well as higher brokerage fees due to increased transactional volume.

a2.MER.reason: Passages state Merrill's advisor-led model earns primarily through fee-based advice (asset management and brokerage fees), complemented by net interest income on client deposits and loans.

a3.MER.label: fact
