a6.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab says it is expanding its branch footprint and hiring hundreds of financial consultants and wealth consultants to deepen relationships with higher net worth retail clients and their families.
items.quote: We're expanding our branch footprint and hiring hundreds of financial consultants and wealth consultants to deepen relationships with our higher net worth retail clients and their families.

items.text: Schwab says it is investing in people and technology to build, deepen, and retain trusted relationships now and for the decades to come.
items.quote: That is why we are investing in both people and technology so we can continue building, deepening and retaining those trusted relationships now and for the decades to come.

items.text: Schwab says it has improved its tax, trust, and estate capabilities and built specialty teams for higher net worth clients.
items.quote: We've improved our tax, trust, and estate capabilities, and we've built out specialty teams catering to the unique needs of our higher net worth clients.

a6.SCHW.reason: These are the firm's stated priorities and strategies for serving wealthy clients and their families across generations.

a7.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab launched the Schwab Teen Investor account for ages 13-17, with a joint account structure that lets parents monitor and engage.
items.quote: We launched the Schwab Teen Investor account, giving young people ages 13 to 17 an engaging way to get started on their lifelong investing journey. Our differentiated joint account structure allows parents to monitor and engage as needed as their teens trade and invest.

items.text: Schwab says it meets young investors in the channels where they seek information, noting they learn about finances primarily through social media and family.
items.quote: One of the reasons they're turning to Schwab is because we're meeting them in the channels where they turn for information about investing. We know they learn about finances primarily through social media and family.

items.text: Schwab says it is active on TikTok and Instagram and is the most followed financial services company on YouTube, going where young investors are.
items.quote: We're all over TikTok and Instagram, and we're the most followed financial services company on YouTube, so we're going to where they are

a7.SCHW.reason: These passages show how Schwab engages next-generation heirs (teen accounts, social media, family-oriented channels).

(EDJ-10K-2025#35); business lines in the count: 'two operating and reportable segments based upon geographic location, the U.S. and Canada' (EDJ-10K-2025#145); not stated: trainees | Merrill (Bank of America Corporation): '(3) Includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.' Net new assets as each firm defines it: Morgan Stanley: 'NNA represent client asset inflows, including interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows, and excluding the impact of business...' (SCHW-10K-2025#119) | Edward Jones: 'Net new assets represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, including fees and commissions and excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions...' (EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#60) | Merrill (Bank of America Corporation): defines a related metric instead: 'The net client AUM flows represent the net change in clients’ AUM balances over a specified period of time, excluding market appreciation/depreciation and...' (RJF-10K-2025#224).

claims.text: Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) projects households will transfer $123.7 trillion to heirs ($105 trillion) and charities ($18 trillion) between now and 2048.
Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) projects Generation Xers will inherit $39 trillion of the transferred wealth.
Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) projects Millennials will inherit $46 trillion of the transferred wealth.
Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) projects women in the Baby Boomer and older generations will receive $40 trillion in horizontal transfers as they outlive their husbands.
Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) projects women in younger generations will receive $47 trillion of the wealth transferred intergenerationally.

Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) estimates most wealth owned by older generations will be donated or passed down to Gen X or Millennial heirs, an estimated total of $85 trillion.
Industry research: UBS (published April 22, 2026) estimates USD 83 trillion in private wealth will change hands globally over the next two to three decades.
Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) projects the wealth transfer will occur between now and 2048.
Industry research: UBS (published April 22, 2026) states the Great Wealth Transfer will occur over the next two to three decades.
Industry research: UBS (published April 22, 2026) states an estimated USD 83 trillion in assets is expected to pass from one generation to the next over the next two decades.

Schwab: On Schwab's 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), the firm stated that roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high net worth and high net worth households, and that it is well positioned to continue serving future generations when that wealth is passed on.
Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) says wealth is now more likely to be held by older households, which will transfer it to heirs and charities.

Industry research: Cerulli (published October 29, 2025) says the next generation (Generation Xers and Millennials) will inherit, while women in Baby Boomer and older generations will receive horizontal transfers and women in younger generations will receive intergenerational transfers.

Industry research: UBS (published April 22, 2026) says wealth is expected to pass from one generation to the next, and the inheriting next generation often begins its involvement earlier through family discussions, governance structures, or growing responsibilities.
Schwab: Schwab's 3Q26 investor deck (period ended September 30, 2026) reports that approximately 75% of assets are retained in a wealth transfer event.

Schwab: On Schwab's 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), the firm said its retention rate around wealth transfers is extremely high and that it is winning assets with all generations.

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's 2Q25 10-Q (period ended June 27, 2025) states that net new assets decreased 10% compared to the second quarter of 2024, continuing a downward trend attributed to higher asset outflows, which are impacted by an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm.
Schwab: Schwab's 3Q26 investor deck (period ended September 30, 2026) describes the firm as built to win across generations.

Schwab: On Schwab's 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), the firm said it is well positioned to serve future generations when wealth is passed on and is winning assets with all generations.

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) describes generational wealth transfer as one of its strategic risks, most notably competition for clients and personnel in light of the evolving financial services industry and generational wealth transfer and changing client demographics, preferences and values.

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) says its continued ability to compete and adapt its business model may be adversely impacted by the evolving financial services industry and generational wealth transfer, including changing client expectations and demographics.

Schwab: On Schwab's 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), the firm said it has improved its tax, trust, and estate capabilities and built specialty teams for higher net worth clients.

The preparation evidence is qualitative and firm-specific, with several firms silent on given aspects, and the only quantitative series (advisor headcount and net new assets) are defined differently across firms and reported over different periods, so the five firms cannot be ranked or compared on a shared basis.

claims.text: Across the five firms, client assets per advisor cannot be validly compared on this evidence: none of the five discloses a client-assets-per-advisor figure, and each firm defines the numerator and the advisor headcount on a different basis. Morgan Stanley's numerator is Wealth Management client assets, which it defines as assets for which Wealth Management provides services (MS-SUPP-2025Q4#35), and its headcount is Wealth Management representatives (MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1). Schwab's numerator is client assets, defined as the market value of all client assets in its custody (SCHW-10K-2025#118), and it reports no financial-advisor headcount, only Form ADV categories such as employees and registered representatives (SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1). Edward Jones reports client assets under care (EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#59) and financial advisors (EDJ-10K-2025#130). Merrill reports Merrill Wealth Management client balances (BAC-SUPP-2026Q3#53) but no Merrill-only advisor headcount: its wealth-advisor figure covers GWIM and Consumer Banking (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), and its Form ADV figures are employees, broker-dealer registered representatives, and investment adviser representatives rather than financial advisors (MER-ADV1A-2026#1). Raymond James reports client assets under administration (RJF-PR-2025-10-22-01#27) and excludes RCS-division advisors from its financial advisor metric although their client assets are included in AUA (RJF-10K-2025#228; RJF-10K-2025#12). Raymond James itself states, "The definitions for client assets may be inconsistent across companies" (RJF-DECK-2025-investor-day#32).

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley disclosed that a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor ("MSVA") is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.
items.quote: If your account is serviced through a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor ("MSVA"), your MSVA is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.

a1.MS.reason: The passage states the base salary component for Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisors.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated that for certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.quote: For certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.scope: Wealth Management and Investment Management revenue-producing employees

items.text: Morgan Stanley attributed higher Wealth Management compensation and benefits expenses primarily to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenue.
items.quote: Compensation and benefits expenses increased, primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenue.

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated that the amount of the fee a client pays is a factor used in calculating the compensation paid to the Financial Advisor, and if the fee rate is below a certain threshold, the Financial Advisor is credited with less than the total fee for compensation purposes.
items.quote: The amount of the fee you pay is a factor we use in calculating the compensation we pay your Financial Advisor. ... If your fee rate is below a certain threshold, we give your Financial Advisor credit for less than the total amount of your fee in calculating his or her compensation.
items.scope: Financial Advisors in the Select UMA Program

items.text: InvestmentNews reported that Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

a2.MS.reason: Passages describe formulaic payouts tied to revenues and a 2027 pay threshold, which are production-based advisor compensation disclosures.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley disclosed that a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.
items.quote: If your account is serviced through a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor ("MSVA"), your MSVA is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.

a3.MS.reason: The passage states the discretionary bonus component for Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisors.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated that deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards, and the programs generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.
items.quote: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated that employees can allocate deferred cash-based awards among a menu of notional investments selected by the Firm, and compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period relevant to each separately vesting portion of deferred awards.
items.quote: Employees are permitted to allocate the value of their deferred cash-based awards among a menu of notional investments... Compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period relevant to each separately vesting portion of deferred awards.

items.text: Morgan Stanley announced it will increase the cash component of its advisor compensation in connection with transitioning DCP hedges to derivatives, to reduce accounting-driven volatility and simplify the compensation program.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. ... these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated that in the first quarter of 2026 it reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.
items.quote: in the first quarter of 2026, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.

a4.MS.reason: Passages describe advisor deferred compensation composition, vesting mechanics, and changes to the deferred proportion.

a5.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated that deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.quote: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.

items.text: Morgan Stanley stated that certain current and former employees, including financial advisors in the Wealth Management segment, participate in the Firm's stock-based compensation plans, which include RSUs, PSUs and an ESPP.
items.quote: Certain current and former employees of the Firm, including financial advisors in the Wealth Management segment, participate in the Firm's stock-based compensation plans. These plans include RSUs, PSUs and an ESPP.
items.scope: Financial advisors in Wealth Management segment

items.text: Morgan Stanley's Equity Incentive Compensation Plan permits awards consisting of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units, performance-based units, and other equity-based or equity-related awards.
items.quote: Awards may consist of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units to be settled by the delivery of shares of common stock (or the value thereof), performance-based units, other awards that are valued by reference to or otherwise based on the fair market value of common stock, and other equity-based or equity-related awards approved by the CMDS Committee.

a5.MS.reason: Passages state advisor participation in stock-based plans and the equity award types available under the plan.

a6.MS.label: fact

items.text: InvestmentNews reported that Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan for advisors and is instead increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. ... Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027...

items.text: A FINRA arbitrator turned aside Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans from an advisor, finding the notes had been paid in full before the hearing.
items.quote: a sole FINRA arbitrator turned aside Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, along with attorney's fees and interest. ... 'The notes originally at issue and related attorneys' fees in this case were paid in full before the hearing...'

items.text: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from a former advisor in a dispute over promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time, and a FINRA arbitrator awarded the firm $8.13 million in damages plus $561,000 in legal fees.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley sued Cohen in 2021 in a dispute over promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time. Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from Cohen. ... The arbitrator ruled Cohen was liable for $8.13 million in damages to Morgan Stanley and also to pay $561,000 in legal fees.

a6.MS.reason: Passages state Morgan Stanley is not introducing 2027 retention bonuses and describe recruiting bonus loans and clawbacks.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that its compensation package includes base pay as a component, along with performance-based incentive pay, equity awards, recognition awards, and health and wellness benefits.
items.quote: Schwab offers a compensation package that rewards both employee and company performance. The package encompasses an array of compensation components in addition to base pay including performance-based incentive pay, equity awards, recognition awards, and a range of health and wellness benefits.

a1.SCHW.reason: Schwab's 10-K states base pay is a component of its compensation package, which is its disclosure about the fixed component of its compensation structure.

a2.SCHW.label: different_quantity

items.text: Schwab said compensation and benefits expense increased for both Investor Services and Advisor Services in the first quarter of 2026 primarily due to annual merit increases, growth in headcount, higher incentive compensation, and higher other employee-related costs.
items.quote: Compensation and benefits expense increased for both segments primarily due to annual merit increases and growth in headcount, higher incentive compensation, and higher other employee-related costs.
items.scope: Investor Services and Advisor Services segments

a2.SCHW.differs_because: States total compensation and benefits expense and its drivers for the segments, not production-based pay, commission schedules, or fee-based payout grids for advisors.
a2.SCHW.reason: No passage states the asked advisor pay structures; this is a related, broader compensation expense disclosure.

first.label: not_found
first.reason: The passages contain no Schwab disclosure about advisor production-based pay, commission schedules, or fee-based payout grids.

a3.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that its compensation package includes performance-based incentive pay as a component.
items.quote: The package encompasses an array of compensation components in addition to base pay including performance-based incentive pay, equity awards, recognition awards, and a range of health and wellness benefits.

items.text: Schwab states that it uses adjusted diluted EPS and return on tangible common equity as components of performance criteria for employee bonus and certain executive management incentive compensation arrangements, with the Compensation Committee maintaining discretion.
items.quote: The Company also uses adjusted diluted EPS and return on tangible common equity as components of performance criteria for employee bonus and certain executive management incentive compensation arrangements. The Compensation Committee of CSC's Board of Directors maintains discretion in evaluating performance against these criteria.

a3.SCHW.reason: Schwab discloses performance-based incentive pay as a compensation component and the performance metrics used for employee bonus and executive incentive compensation.

a4.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that its deferred compensation plan for certain eligible employees permits participants to defer the receipt of certain cash compensation.

Schwab: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that its 2022 Stock Incentive Plan provides for granting stock options and restricted stock units to employees and non-employee directors.

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: Trade press reports (InvestmentNews, published October 26, 2026) that Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan for advisors and is instead increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027.

Merrill: The 2026 Form ADV brochure (published October 30, 2026) states that advisors who join Merrill from other firms generally receive payments in connection with the move, which may take the form of salary guarantees, upfront awards, and compensation contingent on continued employment such as deferred payments and recruitment loans.

Merrill: The 2026 Form ADV brochure (published October 30, 2026) states that the amount paid to advisors under these recruiting arrangements is generally based to a large extent on the size of the business at their prior firm.

Merrill: The 2026 Form ADV brochure (published October 30, 2026) states that future recruiting payments based on assets that transfer are conditioned on the total assets in accounts the advisor services at Merrill, and these bonuses are in addition to the incentive compensation to which advisors are otherwise entitled.

a1.EDJ.label: fact

items.text: For the third quarter of 2025, Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.1%.
items.quote: The Partnership ended the third quarter with 20,429 financial advisors. Financial advisor attrition was 6.1% as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less.
items.definition: Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

items.text: For the second quarter of 2025, Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.4%.
items.quote: Financial advisor attrition increased to 6.4% primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends.
items.definition: Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

items.text: For the third quarter of 2024, Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 4.7%.
items.definition: Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

items.text: For the nine months ended September 26, 2025, Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.0%.
items.definition: Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

items.text: For the nine months ended September 27, 2024, Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 5.1%.
items.definition: Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

items.text: For the second quarter of 2025, Edward Jones said the increase in financial advisor attrition was primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends.

claims.text: Edward Jones: In its 10-Q for the period ended September 26, 2025 (published November 7, 2025), Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.1% for the third quarter of 2025, defining attrition as the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end; it stated, "Financial advisor attrition was 6.1% as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less."

Edward Jones: In its 10-Q for the period ended June 27, 2025 (published August 8, 2025), Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.4% for the second quarter of 2025, defining attrition as the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end; it stated, "Financial advisor attrition increased to 6.4% primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends."

Edward Jones: In its 10-Q for the period ended September 26, 2025 (published November 7, 2025), Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 4.7% for the third quarter of 2024, per its attrition percentage table.

Edward Jones: In its 10-Q for the period ended September 26, 2025 (published November 7, 2025), Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.0% for the nine months ended September 26, 2025, per its attrition percentage table.

Edward Jones: In its 10-Q for the period ended September 26, 2025 (published November 7, 2025), Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 5.1% for the nine months ended September 27, 2024, per its attrition percentage table.

Merrill: On the second-quarter 2026 Bank of America earnings call (published July 14, 2026), CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill adviser attrition is now at near historic lows: "Well, adviser attrition is now at near historic lows. So we're pretty happy with that."

Edward Jones: In its 10-K for the period ended December 31, 2025 (published March 13, 2026), Edward Jones states it "experiences continued efforts by competing firms to hire away its financial advisors, although the Partnership believes its rate of attrition of financial advisors is in line with comparable firms."

Edward Jones: In its 10-Q for the period ended June 27, 2025 (published August 8, 2025), Edward Jones said the increase in its financial advisor attrition in the second quarter of 2025 was "primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends."

Edward Jones vs. Merrill: A numeric comparison of the two firms' financial advisor attrition rates with each other, or with an industry attrition rate, is not valid on this evidence. Edward Jones discloses a quantified, annualized attrition rate (6.1% for the third quarter of 2025 and 6.4% for the second quarter of 2025, under its definition of attrition as the annualized number of advisors who left or retired during the period compared to period-end advisor count), whereas Merrill's attrition is disclosed only qualitatively as being at "near historic lows" (Bank of America CFO, second-quarter 2026 earnings call), and the industry items measure a different quantity—advisors' stated intention to leave their employer within 12 months and advisors expected to retire in the next decade—not an industry attrition rate. Edward Jones's own comparison is limited to its belief that its rate of attrition is "in line with comparable firms."
